quality. * Common Use Cases: Involve classification problems like Fraud Detection, weather forecasting, and customer churn predictions. * Platt Scaling: Involves fitting a logistic regression model to a classifier's output to adjust probabilities. * Isotonic Regression: Uses a non-decreasing function fit to better align predicted and real probabilities. * Histogram Binning: Divides predicted assessment. * Expected Calibration Error (ECE): Measures calibration quality but sensitive to number of bins. * Weather Prediction: Uses calibrated probabilities to provide realistic forecasts. * results.title: How do you evaluate a model’s calibration, and how would you fix a poorly calibrated model? | by NS Academy | Medium
results.content: # **How do you evaluate a model’s calibration, and how would you fix a poorly calibrated model?**. Evaluating and fixing a model’s **calibration** is essential when you care not just about predictions being *correct*, but also about how confident the model is. This is especially important in areas like healthcare, finance, and risk modeling. ## 📏 What is Model Calibration? A model is **well-calibrated** if the predicted probabilities match the actual outcomes. For example, if a model predicts a 0.7 probability of success for 100 instances, about 70 of them should actually succeed. ## ✅ How to Evaluate Model Calibration. * Plots predicted probability (x-axis) vs. actual fraction of positives (y-axis). * A perfectly calibrated model lies along the **diagonal line**. 🔧 Use `sklearn.calibration.calibration_curve` or `CalibrationDisplay`. from sklearn.calibration import calibration\_curve, CalibrationDisplay. prob\_pos = model.predict\_proba(X\_test)[:, 1]. CalibrationDisplay.from\_predictions(true, prob\_pos, n\_bins=10). * Measures the **mean squared error** between predicted probabilities and actual outcomes (0 or 1). * Lower is better; ideal score is 0. from sklearn.metrics import brier\_score\_loss. brier = brier\_score\_loss(y\_test, prob\_pos). Expected Calibration Error (ECE) / Maximum Calibration Error (MCE). * ECE: Weighted average of the absolute difference between predicted and actual frequencies across bins. * MCE: Maximum gap across all bins. (ECE is not built-in in sklearn but can be custom-implemented.). ## 🔧 How to Fix Poor Calibration. * Fits a logistic regression on the model’s output probabilities. * Best for **sigmoid-like miscalibration** (often with SVMs). from sklearn.calibration import CalibratedClassifierCV. calibrated\_model = CalibratedClassifierCV(base\_estimator=model, method=’sigmoid’, cv=5). calibrated\_model.fit(X\_train, y\_train). * Non-parametric; fits a step-wise increasing function. * More flexible, but requires **more** **data** to avoid overfitting. * Works well when calibration is not sigmoid-shaped. calibrated\_model = CalibratedClassifierCV(model, method=’isotonic’, cv=5). Temperature Scaling (For neural networks). * Optimizes a single scalar (temperature) to scale logits before softmax. * Works well for deep learning models. Train with Calibration in Mind. * Use models that are naturally better calibrated (e.g., **logistic regression**). * Avoid overfitting; regularization improves calibration. * Use proper scoring rules like **log loss** in optimization. 2. Evaluate calibration using reliability curves and Brier score. 3. If needed, apply calibration techniques like Platt or Isotonic scaling. 4. Reevaluate to confirm improved alignment of predicted probabilities with **actual outcomes.**.

results.title: Metrics to Measuring Calibration in Deep-Learning | by Sieun Park | CodeX | Medium
results.content: ## CodeX. Everything connected with Tech & Code. Follow to join our 1M+ monthly readers. # Metrics to Measuring Calibration in Deep-Learning. In a previous post, we reviewed the confidence calibration problem in deep neural networks. Informally, confidence calibration means that if a model predicts a class with a 90% probability, that class should appear 90% of the time. We reviewed methods to measure and improve calibration. We also discussed why deep learning typically shows poor calibration performance. The calibration problem is typically visualized using reliability diagrams and the calibration error is evaluated with the expected calibration error. Recent research found that this measure is problematic for 4 reasons, and proposed alternative metrics for measuring calibration error. *This post is based on the paper* *Measuring Calibration in Deep Learning*. ### Expected Calibration Error (ECE). Because calibration can’t be computed directly, we use alternative metrics such as ECE to evaluate the calibration of the network. We first divide the probability interval [0, 1] into multiple *bins*. ECE is calculated as a weighted average of the accuracy/prediction error across the bins, weighted on the relative number of samples in each bin. ECE is commonly used as a scalar metric to evaluate calibration in experiments. But this paper finds that ECE is fundamentally flawed as a metric for…. ## Published in CodeX. ·Last published 8 hours ago. Everything connected with Tech & Code. results.title: uncertainty-calibration · PyPI
results.content: # uncertainty-calibration 0.1.4. Utilities to calibrate model uncertainties and measure calibration. # Uncertainty Calibration Library. This repository contains library code to measure the calibration error of models, including confidence intervals computed by Bootstrap resampling, and code to recalibrate models. Our functions estimate the calibration error and ECE more accurately than prior "plugin" estimators and we provide Bootstrap confidence intervals. See Verified Uncertainty Calibration for more details. Motivating example for uncertainty calibration: Calster and Vickers 2015 train a random forest that takes in features such as tumor size and presence of teratoma, and tries to predict the probability a patient has testicular cancer. Calibration is a popular way to measure the quality of a model's uncertainties, and recalibration is a way to take an existing model and correct its uncertainties to make them better. This library focuses on calibration for classification tasks. Measuring the calibration error of a model is as simple as:. Our library makes it very easy to measure confidence intervals on the calibration error as well, using bootstrap resamples. ## Advanced: ECE, Debiasing, and Top-Label Calibration Error. By default, our library measure per-class, root-mean-squared calibration error, and uses the techniques in Verified Uncertainty Calibration to accurately estimate the calibration error. However, we also support measuring the ECE (Guo et al) and using older, less accurate, ways of estimating the calibration error. get_top_calibration_error(model_probs, labels, p = 1). Multiclass calibration vs ECE / Top-label: When measuring the calibration error of a multiclass model, we can measure the calibration error of all classes (per-class calibration error), or of the top prediction. ## Verified Uncertainty Calibration paper. This repository also contains code for the NeurIPS 2019 (Spotlight) paper Verified Uncertainty Calibration. * The calibration error of methods like Platt scaling and temperature scaling are typically underestimated, and cannot be easily measured. * We propose an efficient recalibration method where the calibration error can be measured. * Experiments showing the debiased estimator can estimate calibration error with fewer samples than standard estimator (Section 5) Running each experiment saves plots in the corresponding folder in saved\_files. uncertainty-calibration-0..gz (15.9 kB view details).
